The clock scan

rotunda
a key-value store: one value per bay, round a clock
scan car
one scan of the store that never stops; the hand of the clock is its roof
robot
a query, its condition on the card
jumping on
a query attaches to the running scan, at any hour
once round
the query sees every value once and detaches where it attached
crate
a query's result: copies with a green tag
ring
the way a query has ridden, seen from above
values read
counted while queries ride: by the one scan, and by a scan per query

As on the slide, the idea comes from the circular scan of QPipe (Harizopoulos, Shkapenyuk, Ailamaki, SIGMOD 2005); the name ClockScan comes from Crescando (Unterbrunner et al., VLDB 2009). There is no clock scan in ExplainDB yet; the notebook Shared-Scan.ipynb shows a shared scan, in which all queries start together. The values are an invented example. The voice is synthetic: Ming-3.0 TTS, voice UK_George.
